title: Derived ringed-topos pullback preserves compatible central scalars
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi, where $A$ and $B$ are sheaves of commutative unital rings, presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Suppose given unital homomorphisms $s_A:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,A)$ and $s_B:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,B)$ such that the structural map $c:u^{-1}A\to B$ carries $u^{-1}s_A(r)$ to $s_B(r)$ for every $r\in R$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] define $(r f)_U(x)=s_A(r)|_U f_U(x)$, and likewise using $s_B$. Equip the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(A),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the induced $R$-linear structures [def-weil-linear-category, lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. The canonical K-flat derived pullback $Lu^*:D(A)\to D(B)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. In particular it sends the endomorphism induced by the actual scalar section $s_A(r)$ to that induced by $s_B(r)$; no flatness of $c$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), K-flat computation and exactness. The compatible-central-scalar assertion is the implicit compatible-central-scalar prerequisite, not a separately stated clause of 06YY.

proof.text: For an $A$-module sheaf $M$, write $\mu^A_M(r)$ for multiplication by $s_A(r)$ on every section. Restrictions commute with this multiplication, and $\mu^A_M(r)$ is $A$-linear because $A$ is commutative. The same assertions hold for $B$. The ring-homomorphism laws for $s_A$ make the abelian group of module-sheaf morphisms an $R$-module. Sectionwise, $g(s_A(r)f(x))=s_A(r)g(f(x))$ for an $A$-linear $g$, so composition is $R$-bilinear. This verifies the stated $R$-linear structures before passing to complexes. On complexes let $\mu_P^A(r)$ be the degreewise multiplication chain map; it commutes with the differentials because they are $A$-linear.

source.place: section-algebra (rings are commutative and modules unitary); sectionwise verification of central scalar actions.

proof.text: Use $u^*M=B\otimes_{u^{-1}A}u^{-1}M$ from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. The algebraic inverse image transports multiplication by $s_A(r)$ to multiplication by $u^{-1}s_A(r)$, by its compatibility with module action and naturality on morphisms [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. On the presheaf tensor product, for sections $b,m$, the balancing relation and the hypothesis on $c$ give $b\otimes(u^{-1}s_A(r)m)=b\,c(u^{-1}s_A(r))\otimes m=s_B(r)b\otimes m$. Thus the two morphisms agree on all pure tensors and hence on their finite sums. Sheafifying this equality gives $u^*(\mu_M^A(r))=\mu^B_{u^*M}(r)$, since the sheaf tensor product and its module action are induced from the presheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Applying this in every degree yields $u^*(\mu_P^A(r))=\mu_{u^*P}^B(r)$ for every complex $P$.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward), pullback formula; scalar equality follows directly from tensor balancing.

proof.text: Put $F=Lu^*$ and write $Q_A,Q_B$ for localization. The induced structures of [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] give $Q_A(\mu_P^A(r))=r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_AP}$ and $Q_B(\mu_{u^*P}^B(r))=r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_Bu^*P}$. If $P$ is K-flat with flat terms, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] supplies the invertible component $\epsilon_P:F(Q_AP)\to Q_Bu^*P$ of a natural transformation on the homotopy category. Apply its naturality to the chain map $\mu_P^A(r)$ and use step 2: $\epsilon_P\circ F(r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_AP})=(r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_Bu^*P})\circ\epsilon_P$. Bilinearity of composition makes the right side equal to $\epsilon_P\circ(r\,\mathrm{id}_{F(Q_AP)})$. Cancel the invertible $\epsilon_P$ to obtain $F(r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_AP})=r\,\mathrm{id}_{F(Q_AP)}$. This uses naturality of the canonical comparison, not an arbitrary objectwise identification.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), canonical natural K-flat comparison; the scalar argument below is supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For an arbitrary complex $K$, take a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Localization makes $a=Q_Ap$ invertible [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In the $R$-linear derived category, $a\circ(r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_AP})=(r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_AK})\circ a$ by bilinearity. Apply $F$ to this equality, substitute step 3, and cancel the isomorphism $F(a)$. Bilinearity in $D(B)$ then gives $F(r\,\mathrm{id}_{Q_AK})=r\,\mathrm{id}_{F(Q_AK)}$. The localization has the complexes as its objects; in any equivalent realization every object is isomorphic to some $Q_AK$. For such an isomorphism $a:Q_AK\to X$, the identical conjugation calculation gives $F(r\,\mathrm{id}_X)=r\,\mathrm{id}_{FX}$. No resolution of a general derived morphism, nor functorial choice of resolutions, is required.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), canonical natural K-flat comparison; the scalar argument below is supplied by the worker.

proof.text: For every derived morphism $f:X\to Y$, bilinearity gives $rf=(r\,\mathrm{id}_Y)\circ f$. Consequently step 4 and functoriality imply $F(rf)=F(r\,\mathrm{id}_Y)\circ F(f)=(r\,\mathrm{id}_{FY})\circ F(f)=rF(f)$. Also $F$ is additive: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] says it is exact as a functor of triangulated categories, and exact functors are additive in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Therefore its maps on all Hom groups are $R$-module homomorphisms, exactly [def-weil-linear-functor]. The special case $f=\mathrm{id}_X$ is preservation of the endomorphism coming from the actual scalar section. The only tensor equality used was balancing, and the derived comparison holds for arbitrary $c$; flatness of $c$ was never needed.
